subject: Traceable Logistics discovery recap — pilot scope, metrics & access
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@traceablelogistics.com>
Cc: Mei Zhang <mei.zhang@traceablelogistics.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Traceable discovery — recap, priority use cases, and pilot onramp

Hi Ethan / Mei —

Great to meet you both today. Quick recap from the call and proposed next steps so we all have the same picture. I kept this intentionally short — please flag anything I missed.

1) Top pain & prioritized use cases- Warehouse returns classification (high volume, ~2.5M descriptions/month) — current false positive rate on automated routing ~18% and manual review is a major cost driver.- Real-time exception triage for carrier anomalies (requires <150ms 95th percentile inference per message).- Unified semantic search across invoices and EDI notes for operations (embeddings-based retrieval).

2) Success metrics for the initial pilot (30 days)- Reduce manual review volume by 30% for returns (measured by ticket counts).- Maintain inference 95th pctl latency <=150ms for per-message scoring.- Embedding-based retrieval P@5 >= 0.78 on the supplied eval set.

3) Proposed pilot scope and plan- Duration: 30 days.- Models: production-distilled LLM for classification + 1536-d embeddings model for search (we'll provide profiles and latency/cost tradeoffs).- Inputs: 1 week of representative sample (anonymized) and a 200-example hand-labeled eval set (you mentioned Mei's team can provide this).- Owners: Traceable: Ethan (product), Mei (data infra). Redwood: Naomi (AE), Ben (Solutions Engineer), Grace (Customer Success).

4) Immediate asks (by next Wed, 3 Jun)- Share a redacted sample CSV (~10k rows) and the 200 eval examples (attach to Drive link or SFTP).- Confirm the infra contact who can create the transient S3 bucket and service account for us to pull samples (we'll only request a read-only key).- Provide any internal constraints (IP, retention) we should include in the MAP.

5) Logistics & docs attached- Call recording and a MAP draft are attached. I also included a tiny data schema sample to speed the onboarding.

Next step: I'll drop a one-page pilot charter and a proposed timeline once you confirm internal stakeholders. Happy to hop on a 20-min technical follow-up next week (Ben will lead).

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0128

Naomi — thanks for the crisp recap. This matches our notes. A few quick confirmations:

- We can provide the 200 hand-labeled evals; Mei will share them by Tues 1 Jun.- I'll ask infra to open a short-lived S3 read-only user and will loop Jordan (infra lead) for credentials.- The returns classification is priority #1. The latency target is aggressive but aligns with the carrier triage use case.

I'll confirm the exact sample size (we have about 2.7M rows for the last 30 days) — will try to get a 10k slice by Monday. We're also OK with Redwood using a staging bucket in our AWS account if that simplifies things.

Appreciate the MAP draft. We'll review and give feedback by early next week. For the technical call, Tue or Wed afternoon PST works for us.

Best,
Ethan

Thanks Ethan — perfect. Two quick clarifications from our side before Ben jumps into the infra checklist:

A) Eval & prompt set- For the returns classifier we'll build a small prompt/eval harness (50 templated prompts + 200 labeled gold examples). Please confirm the label taxonomy (you used: return_accept / return_manual_review / return_reject?). If there's granularity we should preserve, list it.

B) Data retention & scope- We will keep staging data for the pilot only and auto-delete after 45 days unless you request otherwise. If your legal/compliance team has specific retention or redaction rules, let us know now so we can include them in the MAP.

Ben will follow up with a short infra checklist (S3 roles, VPC egress notes, optional presigned URL flow) and a proposed technical timebox for the 30-day run. Would you prefer Ben use DocuSign for the MAP signature or a simple email confirmation?

Best,
Naomi

Subject: RE: Traceable discovery — infra checklist & quick security notes

Hi all — I’ll lead the technical kickoff and wanted to surface the minimal infra checklist so we can avoid back-and-forth during week 1. I kept the asks to the minimum necessary for a read-only onboarding flow.

Minimal onboarding checklist (S3 path preferred)- Temporary S3 bucket/path with lifecycle rule to delete objects after 45 days.- IAM read-only policy and a short-lived access key (we can use an assumed-role flow or presigned URLs if you prefer not to issue keys).- Optional: VPC egress IP allowlist if your infra blocks external egress (we can also deploy via Dedicated VPC in a later phase).- TLS cert & endpoint expectations for any inbound webhooks (not needed in this pilot).

Security notes- Redwood will only request GetObject/ListObject permissions for ingestion. We do not persist credentials after the pilot.- We can sign an NAS/processing addendum if required; small teams often ask for a short SOW addendum for data handling.

Proposed immediate timeline (subject to your confirmation)- Tue 1 Jun: Receive eval set + 10k sample.- Wed 2 Jun: Technical sync (20–30m) — Ben + Naomi + Grace + Traceable infra + data owner.- Fri 4 Jun: Data ingested and initial baseline run complete.- Tue 15 Jun: Wrap-up readout and next steps (if pilot extended).

If the above looks good, Ethan/Mei — can you confirm who will provision the S3 and whether Jordan will be on the sync?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

We prefer DocuSign for the MAP since procurement likes a signed SOW to kick off any vendor work. I'll route internally and get it back to you by next Monday (7 Jun) at the latest.

See you Wed.
